closed.name: Here's Looking at You
closed.why: Closed permanently; last service Friday, June 13, 2025 (end of its 10-year lease), per owner Lien Ta's announcement as reported by Time Out.

closed.name: Yangban Society (later Yangban)
closed.why: Time Out's listing (last modified 2025-05-06) is titled 'Yangban (CLOSED)'; its text describes the same Katianna and John Hong Arts District restaurant as Yangban Society, the name in the 2023 Best New Restaurant semifinalist list.

closed.name: Cassia
closed.why: The restaurant's own site shows a 'Permanently Closed' notice saying Cassia has closed after nearly a decade of service.

closed.name: Esters Wine Shop & Bar
closed.why: The restaurant's own site shows a farewell notice saying Esters has closed its doors after ten years.

closed.name: Mourad
closed.why: Closed in October 2024 (last service Oct. 26, 2024 per SFist, https://sfist.com/2024/10/27/mourad-abruptly-announces-closure-cites-bitter-dispute-with-city-officials-as-one-cause/); Hoodline says the 140 New Montgomery St space has sat empty since.

closed.name: Poltergeist
closed.why: LAist says Diego Argoti's Echo Park barcade restaurant Poltergeist closed in 2024, the same year as his semifinalist nod; he is now cooking as Estrano.

closed.name: Daytrip
closed.why: Announced it was closing in December 2024, citing high costs. The source predates 2025. A May 2, 2025 SFist teaser mentions a 'Daytrip Counter' debuting in Oakland; its relationship to the original restaurant was not checked.

closed.name: Birch & Rye
closed.why: Closing after two years; last night March 30, 2024. The source predates 2025.

closed.name: Birdie G's
closed.why: Moving: its own site says Birdie G's is coming this fall to a new home at Fairmont Century Plaza, 2025 Ave of the Stars, Los Angeles (Century City). The 2024 honor named the Santa Monica restaurant.

notes: Sources: jamesbeard.org announcement pages for semifinalists, nominees (recorded as 'finalist') and winners, 2023-2026. Every California section on those pages was complete: 20 Best Chef: California semifinalists and 5 finalists each year, and all national categories were scanned for ', CA' entries. So the full California list was obtained for all four years; no year is missing. Each stage is its own entry (a winner also has its finalist and semifinalist entries). No level was upgraded. Levels are copied exactly from each page. Categories are the ones in the brief. The 'presented by' sponsor text is dropped from category names. California honors in categories outside the brief were left out of entries: Best New Bar semifinalists (The Halfway Club, SF and Roma Norte, San Diego in 2025; Daisy, LA and The Valley Club, SF in 2026); Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service (2025: Jacob Brown, Lazy Bear, finalist, and Tonya Pitts, One Market Restaurant, semifinalist; 2026: Jack Benchakul, endorffeine coffee bar, finalist, plus semifinalists Paul Einbund, The Morris, and Derek Stevenson, Auro); Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service (2025: Tobin Shea, Redbird, finalist, and Danny Louie, KAIYO, semifinalist; 2026: Kevin Diedrich, Pacific Cocktail Haven, WINNER, and Jason Lee, Darling, semifinalist); and a 2024 Leadership Award nominee, Mai Nguyen (Farmer Mai, Sonoma). Spot-checks against JBF's own past-awards database agree. That database leaves out some stages, for example Buu Ngo / Kru as a 2024 finalist, so the announcement pages are the primary source. America's Classics: there are 16 California honorees from 1998 to 2026. The list comes from JBF's past-awards database, the Algolia index JBFORG_Awards behind https://www.jamesbeard.org/awards/search-past-awards; I checked every Classics record, and 13 records with no state were checked by hand. The years 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2026 are confirmed by JBF announcement or archive pages. The 2023 and 2025 Classics pages list no California honorees. Tadich Grill (1998), Swan Oyster Depot (2000) and Duarte's Tavern (2003) have archive.jamesbeard.org essays that call them America's Classics but don't give the year. Philippe the Original (1999), Langer's (2001), Yuca's (2005) and Taylor's Automatic Refresher (2006) rest on the database record only. The JBF full-list page (/content/americas-classics-award-winners) returns 404. The search page has no per-query URL, so those entries cite the search page itself. Taylor's Automatic Refresher: JBF lists owners Joel and Duncan Gott. The Gott brothers' site (gotts.com/about) says they took over a 1949 Highway 29 roadside stand in St. Helena in 1999; it now operates as Gott's Roadside. Address left null. Naming: restaurant names are as announced, except ABACA->ABACÁ and ANIMAE->Animae (case/accents only). Same-place variants remain: Strong Water Anaheim (2024) / Strong Water (2025); The Harbor House Inn (2023) / Harbor House Inn (2025); Valley Bar & Bottle; Yangban Society. Outstanding Restaurateur entries name the group or restaurants exactly as announced. Their address is null, and the city may list several cities (Cal-India Collective). Friends & Family appears twice and is two different places: Los Angeles bakery (2023 Outstanding Bakery semifinalist) and Oakland (2025 Best Chef semifinalist Gaby Maeda). JBF's Good Food Finder record for the 2025 honor carries the Los Angeles bakery's address, so the Oakland entry's address is null. Addresses: see address_sources. They come from (a) JBF Good Food Finder records (JBFORG_Restaurants, 2025-26 honorees), with typos fixed (Calistgoa, San Fransisco); Sons & Daughters' ZIP 94108 was dropped as inconsistent with 2875 18th St. (b) The restaurant's own site, fetched 2026-10-07 after a robots.txt check. (c) The JBF Classics announcement for Noriega (2011), La Taqueria (2017) and Pho 79 (2019). These older addresses were not re-verified. Some honored restaurants are not closed but have changed: Che Fico was temporarily closed by fire damage (SFist, June 12, 2026, via https://sfist.com/restaurant-closings/). Yank Sing is closing its Rincon Center location (SFist, Sept. 14, 2026); the 49 Stevenson St location remains. Baroo: JBF's chef record marks its old 5706 Santa Monica Blvd site as permanently closed, and the current address is 905 E 2nd St. Cassava's own site now gives 633 Battery St (Jackson Square). Poncho's Tlayudas' site now presents a restaurant called Lugya'h at 4301 W Jefferson Blvd; address left null. Status not verified, not marked closed: Hilda and Jesse (its domain no longer resolves); Le Fantastique (SFist, Dec. 2023: closing 'for now'); Noriega Restaurant and Hotel (its site is JavaScript-only); Lion Dance Cafe (its site lists no location); Swan Oyster Depot, Langer's, SingleThread, Kingfisher, Binchoyaki, Luv2eat, My 2 Cents and Ettan (sites blocked or not found). Bot protection seen and respected: HTTP 403 from kingfishersd.com, singlethreadfarms.com, binchoyaki.com and ettanrestaurant.com, and robots.txt 403 from langersdeli.com, themorris-sf.com, luv2eatthai.com and my2centsla.com. None were retried. Eater, SF Chronicle, LA Times, SFGate, SF Standard and other hosts block ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai, so they were not used. WebSearch calls used: 8, plus 1 rejected before running (duplicate-domain error).
